review_get.title: Retrieve a review by name or identifier

inputSchema.description: Arguments of review_get. The review is resolved inside the current project only: a slug that exists in another project is not found, and no cross-project search happens (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.6).

review.description: Immutable identifier or project-scoped slug, for example bugs-on-homepage.

findings_limit.description: Maximum findings in this page. Defaults to 20 and is capped at the schema maximum.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor (docs/API.md section 6). Its contents are an implementation detail and MUST NOT be parsed by a client.

page_limit.description: Maximum records in one page. Bounded here rather than by the caller's optimism, because an unbounded response is the failure mode docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 13 exists to prevent.

review_include.description: Optional sections of a review response. staleness is deliberately absent: staleness calculation is Stage 2, and a field that would have to be guessed is omitted rather than falsely reported (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 24).

review_selector.description: How an agent names a review: an immutable identifier or a project-scoped slug. Both resolve inside the current project only, and no cross-project search is performed.

review_claim.title: Claim a review for this agent session

idempotency_key.description: Caller-chosen key for a state-changing tool (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 10). It is scoped to actor, tool and project: reuse with the same arguments returns the first result and creates no second record, and reuse with different arguments is refused with IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

identifier.description: Opaque durable identifier (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 3). Consumers MUST treat the value as opaque: the schema bounds only its length and character class and never its documented prefix.

version_number.description: Optimistic-concurrency version. A caller presenting a stale value is refused with VERSION_CONFLICT and the current version in the details (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 11).

review_update_status.title: Move a review to an agent-permitted status

status.description: Requested status. ACCEPTED is not expressible.

agent_review_status.description: Review statuses an agent may request. ACCEPTED is absent by construction, which is the AGENTS.md authority rule expressed as a type rather than as a runtime check. The docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.6 list also named blocked; docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 14 has no such review status and takes precedence, so a blocked agent records the block on the finding it is stuck on.

finding_update_status.title: Move a finding through the agent transitions

inputSchema.description: Arguments of finding_update_status. status is the agent-permitted enumeration, so no argument exists that would ask for a final disposition of a human's finding.

status.description: Requested status, from the section 7.7 list.

resolution_note.description: What was changed and how it was checked. Required to reach FIXED_UNVERIFIED: a completion claim without evidence is refused with EVIDENCE_REQUIRED.

reason.description: Why, recorded on the transition. Required to reach BLOCKED.

agent_finding_status.description: Finding statuses an agent may request, taken from the transition list of docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.7. RESOLVED, WONT_FIX and DUPLICATE are absent: an agent that cannot name a final disposition cannot request one, so the refusal does not depend on a check anybody could forget.

finding_submit_verification.title: Submit verification evidence for a finding

inputSchema.description: Arguments of finding_submit_verification, in the shape of docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.7. The server validates evidence ownership and commit context: an artefact belonging to another project is refused, and a commit equal to the one the finding was captured at is not a fix.

expected_version.description: Version the agent last read, where the agent wants the submission refused if the finding moved.

summary.description: What was changed and how it was checked.

branch.description: Branch the fix was made on. It is checked against the workspace branch where a workspace is known.

commit.description: Commit the fix was made in.

tested_viewports.description: Viewports the fix was checked at.

artefact_ids.description: Evidence. At least one must be a verified screenshot in this project, captured in this project's browser-session lineage.

idempotency_key.description: Key for this submission. A duplicate produces one verification record.

body_text.description: Human-authored or agent-authored prose: a description, instruction, comment, resolution note or verification summary.

branch_name.description: Version-control branch. Recorded on a verification so a human can see which branch the claim was made from.

commit_sha.description: Version-control commit. A verification commit MUST differ from the commit the finding was captured at: a fix cannot exist at the revision the defect was recorded from.

device_scale_factor.description: Device pixel ratio of the capture.

idempotency_key.description: Caller-chosen key for a state-changing tool (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 10). It is scoped to actor, tool and project: reuse with the same arguments returns the first result and creates no second record, and reuse with different arguments is refused with IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

identifier.description: Opaque durable identifier (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 3). Consumers MUST treat the value as opaque: the schema bounds only its length and character class and never its documented prefix.

verification_checks.description: The checks a verification claims to have performed (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 19). They are recorded as claims by the agent and are never treated as proof on their own: the artefacts are the evidence.

reproduced_before.description: Whether the agent reproduced the defect before changing anything.

console_errors_reviewed.description: Whether console output was reviewed after the change.

network_failures_reviewed.description: Whether failed network requests were reviewed after the change.

accessibility_checked.description: Whether keyboard navigation and visible focus were checked.

version_number.description: Optimistic-concurrency version. A caller presenting a stale value is refused with VERSION_CONFLICT and the current version in the details (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 11).

viewport.description: Browser viewport in CSS pixels plus the device pixel ratio. A finding records the viewport it was seen at so it can be reproduced at that size.

device_scale_factor.description: Device pixel ratio the capture was taken at.

browser_take_screenshot.title: Capture verification evidence from a browser session

inputSchema.description: Arguments of browser_take_screenshot. control_epoch is required by docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 7.4 for every browser tool, and a superseded epoch is refused with CONTROL_EPOCH_STALE rather than captured from a browser somebody else now controls.

control_epoch.description: Epoch the agent believes is current.

full_page.description: Capture the whole document rather than the viewport.

purpose.description: Why the capture is being taken. Stage 0 accepts verification only.

idempotency_key.description: Key for this capture, so a retried call does not store two artefacts.

control_epoch.description: Monotonic browser-control epoch (ADR-0007). A command presenting a superseded epoch is refused with CONTROL_EPOCH_STALE rather than executed against a browser somebody else now controls.

idempotency_key.description: Caller-chosen key for a state-changing tool (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 10). It is scoped to actor, tool and project: reuse with the same arguments returns the first result and creates no second record, and reuse with different arguments is refused with IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

identifier.description: Opaque durable identifier (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 3). Consumers MUST treat the value as opaque: the schema bounds only its length and character class and never its documented prefix.

screenshot_purpose.description: Why a capture is being taken. Stage 0 accepts verification only: a capture is evidence, and an unclassified capture cannot be filed under a retention class.

development_services_list.title: List the project's published development services

inputSchema.description: Arguments of development_services_list. It names no project: the project is the session's, and a project argument would be an authorisation input chosen by the caller.

limit.description: Maximum routes in this page, newest first. Bounded here rather than by the caller's optimism, because an unbounded response is the failure mode docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 13 exists to prevent.

page_limit.description: Maximum records in one page. Bounded here rather than by the caller's optimism, because an unbounded response is the failure mode docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 13 exists to prevent.

development_service_publish.title: Publish a local development service through the connector

workspace_id.description: Workspace the development service was started from. It MUST belong to the session's project.

local_host.description: Local address to publish. Defaults to 127.0.0.1, and the connector's own policy still applies (docs/CONNECTOR_PROTOCOL.md section 11).

protocol.description: Protocol the development service speaks. Defaults to http.

ttl_seconds.description: How long the route may live. It is bounded by the deployment's maximum route lifetime, and a longer request is refused rather than clipped: silently shortening a lifetime would make an agent believe it had access it does not have.

idempotency_key.description: Key for this publication. Section 10 requires one on every state-changing tool, and it matters particularly here: a retry without one would open a second tunnel into the development machine for a request the agent believes it made once.

destination_protocol.description: Protocol a development service speaks on its local socket. It is declared at publication and is not negotiable per request.

idempotency_key.description: Caller-chosen key for a state-changing tool (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 10). It is scoped to actor, tool and project: reuse with the same arguments returns the first result and creates no second record, and reuse with different arguments is refused with IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

identifier.description: Opaque durable identifier (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 3). Consumers MUST treat the value as opaque: the schema bounds only its length and character class and never its documented prefix.

local_host.description: Local address of a development service, as a literal IP address. A name would have to be resolved, and a resolver is a rebinding surface (docs/SECURITY.md section 9).

local_port.description: TCP port a development service listens on.

published_service_id.description: Route to revoke. A route outside the session's project is reported absent rather than forbidden (docs/API.md section 5).

idempotency_key.description: Key for this revocation. Section 10 requires one on every state-changing tool; revocation is idempotent in the domain as well, so a retry produces one event either way.

Caller-chosen key for a state-changing tool (docs/MCP_SPEC.md section 10). It is scoped to actor, tool and project: reuse with the same arguments returns the first result and creates no second record, and reuse with different arguments is refused with IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

identifier.description: Opaque durable identifier (docs/DOMAIN_MODEL.md section 3). Consumers MUST treat the value as opaque: the schema bounds only its length and character class and never its documented prefix.
